blocks.text: Lots and land in Moody Park
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Park-street house lots: single-detached houses under the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s.310) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, on the residential streets around the park, with apartment buildings on the 6th Street / 8th Avenue edges under multiple-unit residential districts.

Lot character from the zones: RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5; the edge apartment district RM-1 (s.420) sets maximum site coverage of 40% and density of 35 units per net acre / FSR 1.2. The RS figures are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel (Not verified for any individual lot).

Serviced position, as the City states it: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility and City water / sewer services, and the City's subdivision guide states new lots must be adequately serviced with water, sewers, underground electrical, communications, street lighting, roads, sidewalks and street trees. Servicing for any single parcel is confirmed through that subdivision process — not confirmed parcel-by-parcel here.

ALR vs non-ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve land is identified in Moody Park in the sources read; ALR status for a specific property is a per-address check in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Flood position: the City's floodplain study zones only the city's low-lying edges — Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 west-end Fraser River industrial land, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront and Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area. No floodplain zone for the Moody Park plateau was confirmed; lot-level status is not verified and is a City check.

Market context, labelled correctly: New Westminster is a SnapStats-covered community. SnapStats has no land category, and no detached figure below is a land figure. September 2026 context only: Moody Park sub-area detached inventory 9 / solds 1 (11% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 4 / 0; New Westminster community detached median $1,365,000 and combined condos & townhomes median $560,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (community level only).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Moody Park

items.t: Moody Park is the City of New Westminster neighbourhood centred on Moody Park itself, in the Uptown-west area between 6th Avenue and 8th Avenue; the City lists Moody Park among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, so the City name and the GVR board name match. The working extent is between 8th Avenue, 8th Street, 10th Street and 6th Avenue; precise OCP boundary roads are not verified.
Nearby areas: Uptown to the east, Brow of the Hill to the west, Glenbrooke North to the north, and Downtown and the Quay down the hill to the south.

Roads: 8th Avenue, 6th Avenue, 8th Street and 10th Street, linking to Downtown via 8th Street and Royal Avenue. Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside Moody Park; the nearest are New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) downtown, with TransLink routes 105 (Uptown / New Westminster Station) and 106 (Edmonds Station / New Westminster Station) serving the adjoining Uptown corridors. Commute times in minutes are not verified.

Civic anchors: Moody Park itself (outdoor pool, spray park, sports fields), Moody Park Arena, 701 8th Avenue; the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue, fully opened May 2024; New Westminster Public Library Main Branch, 716 6th Avenue, at the area's east edge; hospital Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, in Sapperton (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Moody Park

items.t: SSMUH / added units: the RS districts allow secondary suites and regulate laneway / carriage houses under Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, within the RS-1 zoning described above. A Moody Park-specific SSMUH unit-count figure on a City source is not confirmed — pull City permits before advertising suite or laneway income on any lot.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Moody Park ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm-class thresholds are not documented in this area's own research, so no farm-class figure is asserted here.

blocks.text: Good to know about Moody Park

items.t: The park is the amenity building: Moody Park itself holds the outdoor pool, spray park and sports fields, Moody Park Arena is at 701 8th Avenue, and the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue fully opened in May 2024 — at 10,644 sq. m. the City's largest capital project to date. Land value on the park streets is amenity value, not density value.

The townhouse zoning exists even though the townhouse stock does not: Bylaw No. 6680's Townhouse District RT-2 (s.410) expressly permits row houses and townhouses, and the OCP carries a Development Permit Area (1.3) for townhouse form — a buyer waiting for new townhouse product on Moody Park land is waiting on rezoning and assembly, not on a missing rule.

New Westminster runs its own electrical utility — City power, water and sewer, not BC Hydro for electricity — a carrying-cost detail that surprises buyers arriving from other suburbs; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a Moody Park house is not verified.

The replacement secondary school is already over capacity: New Westminster Secondary (820 Sixth Street, opened to students January 11, 2021, $106.5 million, 1,900 seats) is SD40's only secondary school and its long-range facilities plan notes it is already operating above capacity — for lot buyers the elementary catchment (Lord Tweedsmuir, with Early French Immersion on site) is the real differentiator between Moody Park addresses.

blocks.text: Moody Park: streets and boundaries

items.t: Moody Park is the neighbourhood centred on Moody Park itself, bounded by 8th Avenue, 8th Street, 10th Street and 6th Avenue in the Uptown-west area of New Westminster — the park is the boundary anchor, not just a feature inside it.
The City name and the board name match: the City lists Moody Park among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, and "Moody Park" is also the sub-area name used in board statistics.
What adjoins it: Uptown to the east, Brow of the Hill to the west, Glenbrooke North to the north, and Downtown and the Quay down the hill to the south.

blocks.text: Moody Park: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is freehold houses on the residential streets around the park, with strata apartment buildings on the 6th Street, 6th Avenue and 8th Avenue edges — the park-facing blocks are houses, the corridor blocks are apartments.

One edge building is confirmed on its property manager's own document: The Diplomat, 707 Eighth Street, strata plan NW920, managed by Quay Pacific Property Management, on the Eighth Street edge of the park.
The neighbourhood's landmark buildings are civic, inside or on the park: Moody Park Arena at 701 8th Avenue and the Moody Park outdoor pool at 701 10th Street.

The replacement New Westminster Secondary School at 820 Sixth Street, at the area's east edge, opened to students on January 11, 2021 — a 1,900-seat building that is School District 40's only secondary school.

blocks.text: Moody Park: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A demolition permit in New Westminster has a heritage step: before a demolition permit is accepted for a building older than 50 years, the City initiates a review of the building to identify any heritage value, and a tree permit application must be submitted with every demolition application.

blocks.text: Moody Park: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Moody Park outdoor pool can be rented privately on weekend mornings in July and August, with City fees starting at $77.62 per hour for up to 30 people — the pool at 701 10th Street is a bookable neighbourhood facility, not just a drop-in one.

New Westminster Secondary School is the district's only secondary school and is already operating above capacity, per School District 40's long-range facilities plan — every Moody Park teenager in the public system is headed to the same building at 820 Sixth Street.
The Main Branch of the New Westminster Public Library is at 716 6th Avenue, at the neighbourhood's east edge in Uptown — inside the Moody Park street grid, not downtown.

The City's floodplain study zones only the low-lying edges of New Westminster — Queensborough, the west-end Fraser River industrial land, the Quay waterfront and the Brunette River industrial area; no floodplain zone is named for the Moody Park plateau, though lot-level status is still confirmed with the City.

Uptown adjoining Moody Park is identified in the Official Community Plan as a Frequent Transit Development Area, which is why the apartment form clusters on the 6th Street and 6th Avenue edges rather than inside the park blocks.

blocks.text: Moody Park: development and new projects

items.t: Seventh Avenue West Corridor — BC Parkway to Tenth Street, City of New Westminster capital project on the corridor along Moody Park's north side; status: active on the City's Projects On The Go list (as of November 3, 2026).

Rotary Crosstown Greenway, 5th Street to 8th Street, City of New Westminster — a greenway segment crossing the Uptown-west grid beside Moody Park; status: active on the City's Projects On The Go list (as of November 3, 2026).

New Westminster Secondary School Cycling Connector — City project linking the school at the area's east edge into the cycling network; status: active on the City's Projects On The Go list (as of November 3, 2026).

təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue — 10,644 square metres with an eight-lane 50-metre pool, leisure pool, fitness centre and gymnasia; status: completed, fully opened May 2024, the City's largest capital project to date.

blocks.text: Moody Park: costs and taxes

items.t: The 2026 city-wide dates a Moody Park owner works to: property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5 percent penalty on current taxes remaining unpaid on July 3, 2026 and a second 5 percent penalty on any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026.
The one facility fee stated on a City page for this neighbourhood: private rental of the Moody Park outdoor pool starts at $77.62 per hour for up to 30 people, on weekend mornings in July and August.

blocks.text: Moody Park: getting around

items.t: No SkyTrain station is inside Moody Park; the working transit link is TransLink route 105 (Uptown / New Westminster Station) and route 106 (Edmonds Station / New Westminster Station) on the adjoining Uptown corridors, feeding New Westminster and Columbia stations on the Expo Line.
8th Street and Royal Avenue are the driving link from the neighbourhood down to Downtown and the Quay; 6th Avenue and 8th Avenue carry east-west traffic across the top and bottom of the park.

The Rotary Crosstown Greenway's 5th-to-8th Street segment and the BC Parkway corridor at Seventh Avenue West are the named cycling routes touching the neighbourhood, both on the City's active projects list.

blocks.text: Moody Park: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check heritage before planning work on an older home: the neighbourhood has a Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement, the City runs a heritage register and permit process, and demolition of a building over 50 years old triggers a City heritage review before a permit is accepted.

Check the tree rules before assuming a lot can be cleared: a tree permit application must be submitted with every demolition permit application in New Westminster, and retained trees on and beside the site are protected during construction.

Check the flood layer anyway: the City's floodplain study names zones only at the city's low-lying edges, but the study is a city-level document — it does not certify any individual Moody Park lot, which is confirmed with the City.

faq.a: No verified one — Moody Park is an established park-side house neighbourhood. Land trades as fee-simple house lots; there is no bare-land subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale lot offering on the verified record.
faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Moody Park?

faq.a: RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) with an FSR cap of 0.5 — the frame a subdivision application is measured against, subject to the Approving Officer process under Bylaw No. 7142, 2007.
faq.q: What is the smallest lot the zoning contemplates here?

faq.a: The RS districts allow secondary suites and regulate laneway / carriage houses under Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 (RS-1: 557.40 m² minimum, FSR 0.5) — a fee-simple second unit on the lot, never a separate strata lot; confirm permits with the City before pricing the income.
faq.q: Can a house lot here carry a suite or a laneway house?

faq.a: No floodplain zone for the plateau was confirmed in the City's floodplain study — its zones are Queensborough, the west-end industrial land, the Quay (Zone 3) and the Brunette River industrial area. Lot-level status is not verified; check with the City.
faq.q: Is Moody Park in the floodplain?

faq.a: School District 40 catchments are set by exact address in the district's school locator. The district operates only one secondary school, and its long-range facilities plan notes that school is already operating above capacity, so the elementary catchment is the real differentiator between Moody Park streets.
faq.q: Which schools serve a Moody Park address?

faq.a: More than a green: the City lists Moody Park with an outdoor pool, spray park and sports fields, and Moody Park Arena stands at 701 8th Avenue at the park. The outdoor pool at 701 10th Street is heated to 27–28 degrees Celsius, has a slide for anyone over 48 inches tall, and stays open in the rain, closing only during lightning events. A few blocks east, the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue fully opened in May 2024 with an eight-lane 50-metre pool.
faq.q: What is actually in Moody Park itself?

faq.a: No — there is no station inside the neighbourhood. The nearest stations are New Westminster Station and Columbia Station on the Expo Line, downtown at the foot of the hill. TransLink route 105 (Uptown / New Westminster Station) and route 106 (Edmonds Station / New Westminster Station) run the Uptown corridors adjoining the area and connect it to those stations, so a Moody Park commute is a bus-to-station trip, not a walk-to-station trip.
faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station in Moody Park?

faq.a: Not without clearing two City steps first: for any building older than 50 years, the City reviews heritage value before a demolition permit is accepted, and a tree permit application must accompany every demolition application under the City's tree protection rules. The neighbourhood's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement means older homes here are documented, so a teardown plan should start with the City's heritage and tree desks, not with a builder's quote.
